newsDocuments.headline: Oil prices rise after attack on Saudi Arabian refinery reignites supply concerns

segments.text: BEIJING: Oil prices rose on Wednesday after an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia , the ​world’s biggest crude exporter, renewed concerns around the ‌risks to supply in the Middle East stemming from the conflict with Iran and its proxies.
Brent crude futures rose $1.48, or 1.3%, to $115.36 a ​barrel as of 0140 GMT.
US West Texas Intermediate ​crude rose $1.22 or 1.22% to $101.12.

newsDocuments.headline: Houthis claim attacks on Saudi oil refinery, defence ministry

segments.text: RIYADH: Yemen’s Houthis said they fired missiles at Saudi Arabia’s biggest oil refinery and its defence ministry on Tuesday as the group kept up its weeks-long wave of attacks.
Saudi Arabia, the world’s top exporter of crude, has suffered constant Houthi strikes against oil and civilian sites this month, including Riyadh’s international airport.
The Houthis said they attacked the defence ministry in Riyadh and the Ras Tanura refinery on the east coast among a series of attacks across the sprawling desert kingdom on Tuesday.

newsDocuments.headline: Palm rises on stronger crude oil, Dalian soyoil

segments.text: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian palm oil futures opened higher on Wednesday after falling for two straight sessions, as stronger crude oil prices and firmer Dalian soyoil supported the market, though weaker palm olein and Chicago soyoil capped the
The benchmark palm oil contract for January delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange gained 21 ringgit, or 0.45%, to 4,722 ringgit ($1,155.37) a metric ton in early trade.

newsDocuments.headline: Gold slips on oil-fuelled inflation fears ahead of Fed meeting

segments.text: Gold prices ticked lower on Wednesday after the previous session’s climb of about 1%, as higher oil prices stoked inflation fears while investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s policy decision later in the day for clues to the rate outlook.
“Gold is moving based on the interest rate expectations and inflation risks because of higher energy prices,” said Soni Kumari, an analyst at ANZ.
Oil prices rose on Wednesday after an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest crude exporter, renewed concerns around the risks to supply in the Middle East.

HOUSTON: Oil futures settled down by almost USD2 a barrel on Tuesday, though prices remain near six-month highs due to the disruption of shipping around the Middle East, and an agreement to end the US-Israeli war with Iran remains elusive.
Brent crude futures settled down USD1.93, or 1.67 percent, at USD113.88 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate crude settled down USD1.86, or 1.83 percent, at USD99.90.

newsDocuments.headline: Russia says three tankers with diesel en route to US

segments.text: MOSCOW: Three tankers carrying Russian diesel are en route to the United States, vessel trackers reported on Tuesday following a Moscow statement, as part of a deal that sparked fierce Ukrainian backlash.

The three ships appear to be the Talisman, which is sanctioned by the US and the European Union; the Leruo, sanctioned by the UK and EU; and the Agioi Fanendes, according to tracking platform Kpler. They are carrying a collective 924,000 ba
US President Donald Trump this month struck an agreement with Russia’s President Vladimir Putin to ease sanctions in exchange for Moscow releasing diesel onto global markets.
